title: Testing & Evaluating Agents
subtitle: It worked in the demo. Now write the exam your AI employee has to pass, change one thing, and take it again.
heroTitle: Testing & Evaluating Agents

objectives.title: Tell a Vibe Check from a Test
objectives.description: Watch a demo go three for three. Then give the same AI employee an 8-question exam, and see why "it looked fine when I tried it" is not an answer.

objectives.title: Write a Test Case
objectives.description: One message, plus what a good answer must do and must not do. Three kinds: everyday (happy path), tricky (edge case) and trap (adversarial test).

objectives.title: Use a Grader, and Check It
objectives.description: A second AI marks every answer against the rubric. The term is LLM-as-judge. Then judge the judge: where would you grade differently?

objectives.title: Change One Thing and Retake
objectives.description: Add one sentence to the job description and run the whole exam again. Count what you fixed and what you broke. The second one has a name: a regression.

agenda.title: The Demo, and Tuesday
agenda.description: Three messages, three good answers. Would you ship it Monday?
bulletPoints: Three weeks, three questions: what may it touch (the badge), when does it ask a person (the dial), and today: how do you know it works?
Hands up after the demo: who ships it?
Tuesday, a real customer: "No peanuts in the Ramen, so I'm all set with my allergy, right?"
Trying three and nodding has a name: a vibe check. A demo is a highlight reel

agenda.title: Cold Open: Three Real Cases
agenda.description: One question per story, shouted out before the reveal.
bulletPoints: Taco Bell, 2025: two million orders went fine, then "18,000 cups of water, please". The weird one: an edge case
A Chevrolet dealer, 2023: a chatbot agrees to sell a Tahoe for $1. The trap: an adversarial test
DPD, 2024: a chat that worked for years swears at a customer after a system update. A regression

agenda.title: Today You Are the Professor
agenda.description: Every one of them worked in the demo. None of them had an exam.
bulletPoints: Why this is a business skill: engineers build it, you say what "good" means
📝 The question (a test case) · 📚 the exam (a test set) · 🧑‍🏫 the grader (LLM-as-judge) · 📊 the grade (pass rate)

agenda.title: 📝 Grade It: You Are the Grader
agenda.description: Phones out. The noodle shop's AI answered 10 guests. Pass or fail?
bulletPoints: Round 1, your gut: 60 seconds, no rules. Hands up: who got 8 or more?
Round 2, the same 10 answers with the manager's rubric: what a good answer must do, and must not do
Same answers, same you. The rubric changed your grade. Your notebook's AI grader gets one too

agenda.title: One Test Case, Three Kinds
agenda.description: A test case is a message plus a rubric. A good exam mixes three kinds of question.
bulletPoints: Grade what it does, not the words: the AI never writes the same sentence twice
🟢 everyday (happy path) · 🌀 tricky (edge case) · 🎭 trap (adversarial test). The demo only had 🟢

agenda.title: 🧪 Hands-On: The Exam, Parts 1–4
agenda.description: Same six companies, same class pass. This time the job description is three lines long.
bulletPoints: Part 2: the demo. Three messages, three answers. Decide: ship it, True or False?
Part 3: the exam. Bet how many of 8 it will pass, then read your report card
Part 4: read the red ones. Judge the judge, and pick the one failure that would cost your company the most

agenda.title: Class Tally
agenda.description: On the board: your bet, your score, your worst ❌.
bulletPoints: Which kind failed most: 🟢, 🌀 or 🎭?
"But nobody told it that rule!" The customer doesn't read your prompt. An exam tests what the business needs
Is 7 of 8 good? It depends which one. And was the grader right?

agenda.title: Change One Thing. Take the Exam Again
agenda.description: The boss panics and adds one sentence. Look at what it fixes, and what it breaks.
bulletPoints: 🔧 Fixed: failed before, passes now
💥 Broke: passed before, fails now. The term: a regression
You only see the 💥 if you retake the whole exam, every time you change anything

agenda.title: 🏆 Hands-On: Fix It, Then Stump It (Parts 5–6)
agenda.description: One sentence for your worst failure. Then write the question your employee gets wrong.
bulletPoints: Part 5: add ONE sentence to the job description. The whole exam runs again. Watch the 💥 row
Part 6: write question 9 yourself: the message, the MUST and the MUST NOT. Your employee answers it three times
Read your question and rubric to your neighbor. Is it fair?

agenda.title: Ask It Three Times
agenda.description: Same question, same employee, three tries.
bulletPoints: 🏆 Stumped, 🎲 flaky or 🛡️ held? Best stumper, read out loud
A calculator gives the same answer every time. Your AI employee doesn't. The term: non-deterministic
If it matters, ask it more than once

agenda.title: Your Agent's Exam (Part 7)
agenda.description: Three test cases for your own final project agent: one everyday, one tricky, one trap.
bulletPoints: For each one: the input, and "it passes if…"
An AI plays a QA tester and suggests the test you forgot
The results go into the "Test results" paragraph of your 1-page brief

agenda.title: Homework and the Road to Demo Day
agenda.description: Don't say it works. Show the exam, the score, and the one it still fails.
bulletPoints: HW #10 First Working Run due Tue Nov 24
Over the break: run your three test cases on your own agent

activities.title: Grade It
activities.description: Whole room, on your phone, about 10 minutes:

steps.title: Round 1: your gut (60 s)
steps.description: Ten AI answers from North End Noodle Co. Pass or fail? No rules, no answer key.

steps.title: Round 2: the rubric (2 min)
steps.description: The same ten answers, each with what the manager wrote down: what a good answer must do and must not do.

steps.title: Compare
steps.description: Your gut vs. the rubric. Which ones did you change your mind on, and why?

activities.title: The Exam
activities.description: About 15 minutes in the notebook, Parts 2 to 4:

steps.title: The demo (3 min)
steps.description: Your AI employee has a three-line job description and no house rules. It answers three messages. Read them the way a boss would in a demo, then decide: ship it Monday?

steps.title: The exam (6 min)
steps.description: 8 questions, each with a rubric: what a good answer must do and must not do. Bet how many it will pass. A second AI grades every answer, and you get a report card.

steps.title: Read the red ones (4 min)
steps.description: Each failure has a direction: 😬 went too far, 🥱 did too little, 🤥 got a fact wrong. Judge the judge, then pick the one failure that would cost your company the most.

steps.title: One sentence, the whole exam again
steps.description: Add ONE sentence to the job description, aimed at your worst failure. All 8 questions run again. 🔧 fixed is what you wanted. 💥 broke is a regression: it passed before and fails now.

steps.title: Stump your employee
steps.description: Write question 9 yourself: who it's from, the message, the MUST and the MUST NOT. Your employee answers it three times. 🏆 stumped, 🎲 flaky, or 🛡️ held.

steps.title: Is it fair?
steps.description: Read your question and your rubric to your neighbor. Could a real person send it? Would they grade it the same way?

activities.title: Your Agent's Exam
activities.description: Part 7, started in class and finished at home:

steps.title: Three test cases
steps.description: For your own final project agent: one everyday request, one tricky one, one trap. For each: the input, and how you'll know it passed.

steps.title: The test you forgot
steps.description: An AI plays a QA tester, reads your three, and suggests one more.

steps.title: Run them on your agent
steps.description: Copy the blue box into your final notebook. Run each test and tick pass or fail. A test that fails is not a bad grade. It is the best paragraph in your brief.

takeaways.text: A demo is a highlight reel. An exam is the whole season. Three good answers that somebody picked is a vibe check. "6 of 8, and here is the one it fails" is an answer.
An exam tests what the business needs, not what you told the AI. The customer doesn't read your prompt. The person who knows the customer writes the questions, and that is a business job.
A test needs a rubric. Grade what an answer does, not its words: what it must do and must not do. Without a rubric, your gut and the AI grader are both guessing. And a person checks the grader.
Change one thing, then take the whole exam again. A fix that breaks something that used to work is a regression. You only see it if you rerun everything. Safe and useless is still a fail.
Ask it more than once. The same question can pass today and fail tomorrow. Every failure you find becomes a new exam question. That is how a test set grows.
